gen-dafont-bloody-gf-ruda: Bloody lets its big round lowercase bowls do the shouting, heavy and commanding from the first letter. And Ruda keeps a wire-thin monoline skeleton and a sizable x-height, which makes it the one that actually carries the reading.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-saira: Saira reads rounded and tall, each s left with a gap you can see through, nothing fussy about it. Bloody takes the loud, commanding work; Saira just gets on with the plain sans job.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-sarpanch: Those big round lowercase bowls are what you notice first in Bloody, and they give it a commanding, bloody swagger. Sarpanch follows in contemporary sans-serif, with a clearly open e and a compact gap up to the ascender line.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-savate: Bloody arrives with big round bowls and a commanding, bloody attitude that fills the space above. But Savate answers in sans-serif, with open jaws on every curve and a tall o nearly matching its capital.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Big round lowercase bowls give Bloody its commanding, slightly menacing face, and they dominate whatever sits near them. Yet Schibsted Grotesk stays approachable in sans-serif, with tall-bowled e and a shapes and terminals that never close in.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-sen: Sen is built tall, tracing each letter with a constant marker-nib line, and its curves stop before turning inward. Yet Bloody brings the commanding punch, so the two are easy to tell apart at a glance.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-sintony: Chunky and tall through the middle, Sintony reads smooth, with no clogged curves anywhere along a line. Bloody's big round bowls take the loud part, and the plain sans keeps going quietly beneath it.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-sofia-sans: Sofia Sans reads modern and rounded, with a clearly open side on its letters and tall lowercase like cut acrylic stencil pieces. Bloody's big bowls are the loud counterpart, while the sans draws every glyph with an unmodulated line.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-sofia-sans-semi-con: Clean is the mood Sofia Sans Semi Condensed gives off, with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. And its constant weight and big visible curve entrances keep lines easy to follow, while Bloody stays commanding up top.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-sono: Bloody is all commanding, bloody weight, with big round lowercase bowls that make a loud entrance when set large. Sono sits beneath with wide spacing and tall lowercase.
